text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 2.6% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 8.3%. The pullback appears tied to a broad unwinding of the refinery trade—a CNBC report on November 23rd explicitly called out that "the epic boom in refinery-related stocks is unwinding," suggesting investors are rotating out of energy companies that benefited from high refining margins. While U.S. oil prices remain solid at $89.53 per barrel and U.S. refineries are running at a healthy 95.7% capacity, the trade's momentum has broken.

The broader context adds pressure: climate negotiations collapsed over the weekend with no meaningful fossil fuel commitments, and ongoing Middle East tensions—including Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries—are creating uncertainty rather than the sustained supply tightness that fueled the refinery boom earlier this year. The shift in investor appetite away from energy stocks is outweighing the fundamentals that once drove the sector higher.
